q: Oxidation numbers have a variety of uses in chemistry- from writing formulae to predicting properties of compounds and assisting in the balancing of ____ reactions in which electrons are transferred.
e: Oxidation numbers have a variety of uses in chemistry- from writing formulae to predicting properties of compounds and assisting in the balancing of oxidation-reduction reactions in which electrons are transferred. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: The ____ (or oxidation state) of an atom can be zero, positive, or negative.
e: The oxidation number (or oxidation state) of an atom can be zero, positive, or negative. Free elements are assigned oxidation number 0, whether the molecule is monoatomic or diatomic. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: All elements in their free state (uncombined with other elements) have an oxidation number of ____.
e: All elements in their free state (uncombined with other elements) have an oxidation number of zero. Free elements are assigned oxidation number 0, whether the molecule is monoatomic or diatomic. An uncombined element in its free state has oxidation number zero. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion.

q: A positive oxidation number means the atom has ____ electrons assigned to it than in the neutral atom.
e: A positive oxidation number means the atom has fewer electrons assigned to it than in the neutral atom. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: A negative oxidation number means the atom has ____ electrons assigned to it than in the neutral atom.
e: A negative oxidation number means the atom has more electrons assigned to it than in the neutral atom. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: The oxidation number of an atom that has lost or gained electrons to form an ion is the same as the positive or negative ____ of the ion.
e: The oxidation number of an atom that has lost or gained electrons to form an ion is the same as the positive or negative charge of the ion. A positive oxidation number means that atom is assigned fewer electrons than the neutral atom. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion.

q: All elements regardless of whether they are monoatomic, diatomic or triatomic have an oxidation number of ____.
e: All elements regardless of whether they are monoatomic, diatomic or triatomic have an oxidation number of zero. Free elements are assigned oxidation number 0, whether the molecule is monoatomic or diatomic. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: The algebraic sum of the oxidation numbers of the atoms in a neutral molecule is ____.
e: The algebraic sum of the oxidation numbers of the atoms in a neutral molecule is zero. Free elements are assigned oxidation number 0, whether the molecule is monoatomic or diatomic. In a neutral molecule the oxidation numbers of all atoms add up to zero. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion.

q: The algebraic sum of the oxidation numbers of the atoms in a polyatomic ion is equal to the ____ on the ion.
e: The algebraic sum of the oxidation numbers of the atoms in a polyatomic ion is equal to the charge on the ion. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: Oxidation number of H is ____, except in metal hydrides, where it is -1.
e: Oxidation number of H is +1, except in metal hydrides, where it is -1. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: Oxidation number of H in metal hydrides is ____.
e: Oxidation number of H in metal hydrides is -1. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: Oxidation number of O is ____, except in peroxides and in $OF_2$.
e: Oxidation number of O is -2, except in peroxides and in OF_2. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom. Oxygen is usually -2, except in peroxides (-1) and in OF2 (+2).

q: Oxidation number of O in peroxides (e.g., $H_2O_2$, $BaO_2$, $Na_2O_2$) is ____.
e: Oxidation number of O in peroxides (e.g., H_2O_2, BaO_2, Na_2O_2) is -1. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom. Oxygen is usually -2, except in peroxides (-1) and in OF2 (+2).

q: Oxidation number of O in $OF_2$ is ____.
e: Oxidation number of O in OF_2 is +2. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom. Oxygen is usually -2, except in peroxides (-1) and in OF2 (+2).

q: The metallic element in an ionic compound has a ____ oxidation number.
e: The metallic element in an ionic compound has a positive oxidation number. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: Alkali metals in combined state have an oxidation number ____.
e: Alkali metals in combined state have an oxidation number +1. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: Alkaline earth metals in combined state have an oxidation number ____.
e: Alkaline earth metals in combined state have an oxidation number +2. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: The oxidation number of halogen in compounds (e.g., $BaCl_2$, $NaBr$, $KI$) is ____.
e: The oxidation number of halogen in compounds (e.g., BaCl_2, NaBr, KI) is -1. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: In covalent compounds, the negative oxidation number is assigned to the more ____ atom.
e: In covalent compounds, the negative oxidation number is assigned to the more electronegative atom. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom. A covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons between atoms.
